benchmark.description: S3 bucket + Glue DB for benchmark results

registry.description: Model Package Group + AI Registry Hub + policies

training.description: Artifacts bucket (tune/train/optimize output + MLflow store) + legacy training/adapters buckets + reward-Lambda role + MLflow experiment tracking

eks.description: Provisions a standalone EKS environment: VPC, EKS cluster, OIDC provider, Fargate profile, CSI/metrics add-ons, and the EKS inference IRSA role. Vanilla-EKS users add this alone; the hyperpod module depends on it.
eks.estimatedMonthlyCost: $73+/mo (EKS control plane; NAT + compute billed separately)

hyperpod.description: DEPRECATED (v2.0.0) — HyperPod CLUSTER PROVISIONING is deprecated pending a dedicated spike (BL153). The live BL143 rehearsal proved MLCC's cluster-creation path does not enable inference at CreateCluster time (the cluster comes up with no InferenceConfig), so the operator can never create a SageMaker endpoint — a root cause that lives in AWS's compiled provisioning Lambda and cannot be cleanly reconstructed here. Provision a HyperPod cluster via the AWS SageMaker console / published CFT instead; the `hyperpod-eks` DEPLOY target still works against a correctly-provisioned cluster. See docs/architecture/eks-hyperpod-migration.md.
hyperpod.estimatedMonthlyCost: ~$1,300/mo (2 x ml.c5.4xlarge on-demand CPU default-worker floor, billed 24/7 while provisioned; confirm current rates on the SageMaker pricing page. GPU model-serving instances are billed separately only when attached. Remove the module when idle)
hyperpod.deprecationNote: Cluster provisioning deprecated pending the HP-native spike (BL153) — it does not enable inference at CreateCluster time, so model endpoints are never created. Provision via the AWS console/CFT; deploy with --target hyperpod-eks against the result. See docs/architecture/eks-hyperpod-migration.md.
